text:
Marek: heads-up — seeing long-run memory growth on the KV layer when serving sessions with long histories (~200k tokens). profiler shows pages not getting recycled and some requests re-reading stale blocks across sessions. attaching quick dump.
Alyssa: ugh. is this the same alignment leak we saw last quarter or something new?
Marek: different pattern — tokens shift by 1-2 positions when fragments are reused which corrupts tag boundaries. not a pure offset leak, looks like a misapplied slot index during free/alloc path.
Emily: can you paste the relevant log snippet? log correlation id would help.
Marek: sure — here's the stream from a failing run:
```
kv: alloc slot=42 page=7 offset=8192 tag=0x1a2b
kv: write fragment len=512 tokens=64 req_id=0xdeadbeef
kv: free slot=42 req_tag=0x0
kv: alloc slot=42 page=7 offset=8208 tag=0x1a2b
kv: read fragment len=512 tokens=64 req_id=0xfeedface -> aligned_offset mismatch
```
Marek: note free sets req_tag=0 but we still reuse slot without clearing request_id or zeroing stale tag payload in the page buffer.
Zhen: that explains cross-request contamination — I saw a ReplayFailure in qa that matched this: older request's fragment returned in new request when sequence lengths differed.
Jon: repro steps? I can run locally if you give a minimal script.
Marek: repro is pretty small:
- create session A with context ~120k tokens, do repeated incremental generations to fill multiple pages
- create session B with short prompts that trigger reuse of the same slot ids
- observe B getting token sequences that include suffixes from A
Example curl loop I used:
```
for i in 1..50; do curl -X POST /v1/generate -d '{"session":"A","input":"long..."}'; done
curl -X POST /v1/generate -d '{"session":"B","input":"hi"}'
```
Alyssa: are we sure it's not a kernel/batching timing artifact? could concurrent reuse + delayed eviction produce this without a logic bug?
Emily: I profiled the allocator in that run — contention spikes but the real culprit is the slot lifecycle: we only clear the "owner_request_id" on reclaim in the fastpath when eviction_count > 0. if eviction_count==0 (hot rotate) we skip the full cleanup.
Zhen: so hot-rotate path is leaving stale payload in the page and not resetting alignment metadata. easy to trigger with churned long contexts.
Jon: mitigation idea — on reclaim always memzero the header region (cheap) and set owner_request_id to 0; cost is extra memcpy on hot path though.
Marek: agreed. short-term mitigation: add a feature flag to disable fast hot-rotate reuse for sessions flagged as long_context (threshold 64k tokens). that reduces reuse but prevents contamination while we fix.
infra-bot: deploy check: canary 2 already rolled to us-east. will hold next rollout until PR merged and smoke-tested.
Alyssa: ok planning — Marek to open PR with minimal header-zero fix + unit test that asserts no cross-session reads; Zhen to add repro harness to perf/lab for e2e reproduction; Emily to benchmark hotpath regression (<5% P95 increase target).
Marek: will open PR in ~1h. putting a note in the runbook and tagging owners. cc @Jon for smoke runs.
Jon: can run smoke after PR merge. also add a fuzz test to allocator to randomize request_id and ensure no carryover.
Marek: thanks all. tracking in #issue-kv  -- will paste PR link when created. :thumbsup:
